params.body:
One blue-grey family in two weights, as tokens in `@theme`, and every `gray`,
`zinc` and `slate` class in the repo renamed onto it. `docs/design-system.md`
writes down where the colour comes from and what stays off limits.

## Where the colour comes from

Naviskore is used by athena, which belongs to xplora, and it has to be able to
serve a next school group without looking like the first one's in-house tool.
So the palette is derived, not chosen. Athena and xplora share exactly one
thing: a deep blue on practically the same hue (xplora `#253242` at 254.0,
athena `#11437f` at 255.8). Both ramps sit on hue 255, washed out: athena's
navy carries chroma 0.114, the chrome here stays under 0.04. Blue-grey, not
navy. `primary` is the same hue a step firmer (chroma 0.09) and only goes on
what can be clicked.

## What stays off limits

`App\Enums\ValueColor` gives five colours a meaning about a student: red is
score 1, orange 2, green 3, **blue 4**, grey absent. Those hex values are on
printed report cards of past school years and do not move here; only the
on-screen class strings in `tailwindClasses()` follow the rename. The score
blue is vivid (chroma 0.21) on hue 262; `primary-600` is a quarter of that.
The doc says: never the two in the same role.

## The rename

`gray` appeared 713 times, `zinc` 577, `slate` 39, all three on the same
screens. Renamed mechanically to `ink-N`: **1,335 classes in 125 files**, by a
word-boundary regex over `resources/` and `app/`, nothing hand-edited. Both
ramps use Tailwind's own lightness steps for `gray` (98.5% down to 13%), which
is the reason this is safe: equal steps mean every text and rule keeps its
contrast exactly, only the tint moves. The old `primary` (an alias of `sky`,
used in nine places) becomes the blue-grey.

The report snapshot tests failed after the rename, as they should: score DTOs
carry `tailwindClasses`. Regenerated with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, then checked
that every changed line in the 24 snapshot files differs only by the class
name. Nothing else in a report moved.

## Two derived images

`naviskore.png` is black art on opaque white, so it can only ever be black on a
light ground; `filter: invert()` turns the inside of the compass black and
yields a black arrow on a white disc. Two files fix that, both generated from
the original, not redrawn:

- `naviskore-inkt.png`: the ink moved into the alpha channel. As a CSS mask on
  a coloured box the mark takes any colour on any ground.
- `naviskore-kompas.png`: the compass alone, square, cut at the empty row
  between compass and wordmark (y = 308), for watermarks.

The login page that uses them is a separate pull request on top of this one.

## Checks

- `php artisan test`: 196 passed, 1 failed (`BuildStampTest`, which needs a
  full clone rather than a worktree). Snapshot suite and `ValueColorTest` green.
- `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: no errors. `vendor/bin/pint --test`: passed.
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint`: 0 errors, the 12 pre-existing warnings.
params.title: Het design system: één blauwgrijze familie, en gray/zinc/slate worden ink
